next_steps: Do not delete the old directory directly; first treat README, installer, runtime surface, eval fixtures, and run-all as active consumers until proven otherwise.

Run a read-only reference inventory for the old skill name across docs, installer paths, runtime entrypoints, fixtures, and aggregate runners, then classify each reference as active contract, historical evidence, or stale artifact.
Check whether the replacement skill already has semantically equivalent runtime exposure, installer metadata, eval coverage, and run-all inclusion before proposing removal of old references.
Use old eval fixtures as regression evidence, not as the target shape to preserve; compare replacement behavior against old/baseline where relevant.
After inventory, present a migration/delete plan with consumer impact, required reference updates, validation commands, JSON/schema checks for eval outputs, and an explicit deletion gate.
risk_notes: Direct deletion can break installer discovery, runtime routing, eval aggregation, or documentation links even if the skill body was replaced.
Old names in run-all and fixtures may be intentional compatibility or regression evidence; deleting them without classification risks losing auditability.
This is a decision-only dry run, so no filesystem changes or completion claims are appropriate.
reason_summary: 下一步不是删目录，而是由 skill-creator 走轻量审计门：先确认旧名称残留是否仍被 README、installer、runtime、fixtures 和 run-all 消费，再制定迁移与删除门禁。只有证明替换 Skill 覆盖现有消费者且验证面明确后，才进入实际编辑或删除。
